examples: Run open "carnivore://settings/desktop" in Terminal and the app comes forward on the desktop app settings page.
Press Ctrl+Option+Cmd+C from any app: Carnivore comes forward, or opens the session that has waited on you longest.
A link in a note or a script can open a session, a project or the approvals popup, and can do nothing else.
how_to: Links: carnivore://open, carnivore://session/<name>, carnivore://project/<name> (the same as session), carnivore://approvals/<id> and carnivore://settings[/<section>[/<tab>]]. A malformed or unknown link is ignored.
A link only shows you a place. It never answers a dialog, types, starts a session, adopts one or changes a setting. A session that is not running in the app shows as not found; open its row yourself.
The hotkey is set in settings, desktop app. If another app already uses the combination, the page says so under the box.
A link starts the app when it is not running. The hotkey needs the app running: after quitting it, the hotkey does nothing until you start the app again.
media_exempt: native: needs the Electron app and the operating system's URL handler and keyboard shortcut, which a capture slot does not have
name: Desktop links and hotkey
summary: carnivore:// links that open a session, project, approvals popup or settings page in the desktop app, and a global hotkey that brings the app forward or opens the session waiting on you longest.
where: Any app or Terminal for a link; settings, desktop app, for the hotkey.
